newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Senate approves welfare limits, job guides.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Senate approves welfare limits, job guides.

text.p: - The New Jersey Senate Monday voted to impose a five-year lifetime limit on welfare benefits and set administrative guidelines requiring most welfare recipients to find a job within two years.
The two bills completed New Jersey's Work First welfare reforms, although the Whitman administration has used its emergency powers to operate under the new guidelines since Feb 1.

The use of emergency powers enabled New Jersey to meet deadlines written into the federal welfare reform law and to protect its waivers and block grants, according to Human Services Commissioner William Waldman.
An administration official said Whitman would sign the legislation.

"Might there be technical glitches? That's what the technical review by the governor's counsel will determine," said Whitman spokesman Peter McDonough. "But these bills should be signed after that review."
"What we've done here is say, 'Work is important,'" said Sen. Wayne Bryant, a Camden County Democrat who helped the Republican governor rework the welfare reform enacted in 1991, which he developed.

The primary change voted by the Assembly was to require welfare clients to be paid minimum wage in their 20 hours a week of work. It also covered welfare clients injured on the job with worker's compensation.
--Provides day care and Medicaid coverage for two years after the welfare recipient starts work.
--Requires 14 and 15-year-olds with children to live with their parents, who will manage their benefits.
--Grants a six-month extension of benefits for people who satisfy the search requirements but cannot land a job.
--Allows for benefits to welfare families with a step- parent.
--Protects the benefits of legal immigrants by using state funds.
--Requires welfare workers to work out a plan to achieve self-reliance for each recipient.
